title: Cobra: commands, flags, help and autocompletion

videos.script: Lesson 1 built hits with nothing but the standard library. It worked, and it left a list of things undone. A typo got no suggestion. Help covered the whole program, never one command. And the Tab key did nothing. This lesson hands that list to Cobra. {{tree}} First the shape. With Cobra, a command line is a tree of values. The root is hits, and count and top hang below it. Cobra reads the words, walks down the tree and runs the command it reached. {{flags}} Then the flags. Some belong to one command, and some reach every command below. Flags may now come after the file name, the way most Linux tools accept them. {{errors}} Next, the mistakes. Cobra writes the help and suggests count when you type cont. But it never chooses an exit code. So hits keeps lesson 1's promise itself: zero, one or two, each meaning one thing. {{tab}} Last, the Tab key. The shell asks hits what to offer, and you can ask it the same question by hand. {{cost}} None of this is free. The binary grows by about a megabyte, and the lesson measures exactly what you paid for.
